blogs.title: Beyond the GI Tract: When GLP-1 Agonists Trigger Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy
blogs.description: This post analyzes the distinction between common GLP-1 induced rhabdomyolysis (direct toxicity) and the rare, delayed onset of Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy (IMNM). We will explore why this specific case represents a paradigm shift from simple muscle breakdown to an autoimmune process, highlighting the critical difference in timeline (acute vs. progressive over months) and the necessity of immunosuppression rather than just drug cessation.

blogs.title: The Seronegative Trap: Diagnosing IMNM Without Classic Autoantibodies
blogs.description: Focusing on the diagnostic challenge presented in this case, this article discusses the reality that ~30% of IMNM patients are seronegative for classic markers like anti-HMGCR or anti-SRP. We will review how to navigate a negative myositis panel when clinical suspicion is high, emphasizing the pivotal role of muscle biopsy findings (necrosis with minimal inflammation, MAC deposition) and clinical context in establishing a diagnosis of drug-induced IMNM.

blogs.title: One Dose Away: Unraveling the Temporal Relationship Between Semaglutide and Autoimmunity
blogs.description: While most drug-induced myopathies require chronic exposure, this case presents a unique 'single-dose' trigger hypothesis. This blog explores the concept of molecular mimicry or epitope spreading triggered by a single exposure in a genetically susceptible host. We will discuss how to apply WHO-Uppsala Monitoring Centre causality criteria to link a solitary event to a disease process manifesting four months later, challenging traditional timelines for adverse drug reactions.

blogs.title: Decoding Elevated Liver Enzymes and Troponin: Don't Miss the Muscle!
blogs.description: This educational piece focuses on the 'red herrings' in this case: elevated AST/ALT and cardiac biomarkers. We will teach clinicians how to differentiate hepatic steatosis from muscle-derived enzyme leakage (the AST>ALT ratio nuance) and distinguish true myocarditis from stress-induced cardiomyopathy or skeletal muscle contamination in troponin assays. The goal is to prevent misdiagnosis when systemic weakness coincides with multi-organ lab abnormalities.
